definition: The task of identifying harmful, offensive, or abusive content in text, often using a dedicated classifier model.
details: Toxicity detection models are commonly used as part of content moderation pipelines to filter inputs or outputs in AI applications, though they can struggle with context-dependent nuance, sarcasm, or reclaimed language.

explainer.lead: Toxicity detection is the task of identifying harmful, offensive or abusive content in text, often with a dedicated classifier model. It matters because content moderation pipelines rely on it to filter inputs and outputs in AI applications.

tiers.eli5: It is a filter that reads text and flags the mean, hateful or abusive parts, like a referee watching what people say.
tiers.practitioner: These models are commonly used inside content moderation pipelines to filter inputs or outputs in AI applications. A pitfall is that they can struggle with context-dependent nuance, sarcasm, or reclaimed language.
tiers.paperLevel: Toxicity detection is the task of identifying harmful, offensive or abusive content in text, typically using a dedicated classifier model. Known limits include difficulty with context-dependent nuance, sarcasm and reclaimed language.

explainer.example: A chat application runs user messages through a toxicity classifier before display, flagging a message whose tone is abusive.
